In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the JPEG algorithm is the most efficient one to be used in a recording service for the development and testing of real-time image processing systems.
the compression algorithms are a very useful tool for developing and testing real-time image processing systems.
the compression of images for the purpose of recording them in the production line is not an efficient solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the JPEG 2000 compression algorithm provides the best results in terms of the compression ratio and CPU time.
the use of the image compression algorithm based on wavelet transforms is the most suitable for the development and testing of the real-time imaging systems.

the use of JPEG2000 is recommended when the CPU time is not critical and the image size reduction is important, whereas for real-time applications JPEG2000 is not recommended because it is too time consuming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CPU time to compress a single image is not a good indicator of the performance of a compression algorithm for a real-time recording.
the compression level of the images must be selected in function of the processing time required by the algorithms to process the images.
the CPU time required for the compression process can be reduced by a factor of 10 with a loss in image quality of only 2% when using the JPEG algorithm.
